newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds and futures lose footing, track T-bonds down.
newsitem.headline: Bunds and futures lose footing, track T-bonds down.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were cautious in early business on Tuesday, swiftly turning tail from a slightly higher opening and dipping into negative ground after the first hour trade.
Dealers said the market was tracking developments in U.S. Treasuries, which softened in Tokyo overnight ahead of a key inflation release due this session.

By 0720 GMT, the DTB June future was trading five basis points lower on the day at 102.16, having been as high as 102.24 just after the open. The 10-year benchark cash Bund was yielding 5.717 percent at a bid price of 102.09.

Domestic data showing final April consumer price inflation at 1.4 percent year on year would provide background support for the market as it confirmed a view that interest rates will remain steady for some time, analysts said.
But since the data were widely expected, any immediate impact would be muted, they said.
"The CPI was pretty much in line, so it really did not have much effect on prices," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Coopertaive Bank in London.
"The market had a good rally yesterday. Now its moving into a consolidation phase and we may see a bit of that given back."
The DTB June Bund contract skipped up to a high at 102.32 late on Monday, the market's highest level since early March, and traders said it may need to take a breather this session to consolidate.

But they said there was firm support on the downside at 102.00 and, barring any shocks from the U.S., the contract should hold above there. "We'll have to see what the retail sales bring us later," said a trader.
Economists polled by Reuters are forecasting a drop in April retail sales of 0.3 percent on the month after a 0.1 percent gain in March.
In the cash market, the 10-year Bund/T-note yield gap was steady at 106 basis points bu 0743 GMT.
